useful_references.title: Solutions to the 85th William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition
useful_references.complete_statement: For B2: No, there is no such sequence; any sequence of convex quadrilaterals in which consecutive terms are partners must be finite.
expanded_definitions: The center O is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the two diagonals of a convex quadrilateral.
applicability_check: Convexity ensures the diagonals intersect and hence are nonparallel, so their perpendicular bisectors have a unique intersection.
For a partner move, a direct distance argument, rather than an imprecise claim that the entire other diagonal reflects, proves O remains the new diagonal-bisector intersection.
proof_insights: The distances from O to the four vertices and the side-length multiset remain invariant.
Finite choices of triangle side lengths around O force finitely many congruence classes.
useful_references.why_useful: It supplies the decisive finite-state invariant; the submitted proof will prove every step self-containedly.
